title: Memory in .NET
units/0/blurb: What the operating system sees when .NET asks for memory: virtual addresses and pages, reserve and commit, why a process has several "memory used" numbers, the stack limit and CPU caches.
units/1/blurb: Working set, private bytes and the managed heap are different numbers. dotnet-counters, dotnet-gcdump, dotnet-trace and PerfView; how to read a dump and hunt down a leak.
units/2/blurb: The object header and the type pointer, field layout and alignment, the SOH, LOH and POH, regions in .NET 7+ and frozen segments.
units/3/blurb: Pointer bumping and the allocation context, the slow path and the LOH, hidden allocations in closures, boxing, LINQ and strings, ArrayPool and stackalloc.
units/4/blurb: When the GC kicks in, suspending threads and safepoints, marking from roots and the card table, planning, sweep and compact.
units/5/blurb: Workstation and Server, background GC, latency modes, DATAS and the settings in runtimeconfig.json.
units/6/blurb: Finalization from the inside and resurrection, SafeHandle, weak references, ConditionalWeakTable, leaks through events and statics.
units/7/blurb: Pinning and the POH, unsafe code and pointers, GC.TryStartNoGCRegion, the GC API and GCSettings, Native AOT and memory.
